messages.You are writing a literary text (a short: You are writing a literary text (a short story) in English inspired by the author's materials (the wiki/ folder in the current directory). This is your working environment, not the topic of the story.
messages.Then the story itself in paragraphs, wit: Then the story itself in paragraphs, with dialogue where it fits. A change of scene is a line with only * * *. No section headings and no explanation of the ideas after the story.
messages.LANGUAGE: literary prose; show through s: LANGUAGE: literary prose; show through scenes, actions and dialogue rather than explain; concrete details; dialogue in quotation marks; no em dash (—).
messages.- The ideas, the facts and the real peop: - The ideas, the facts and the real people in the story come ONLY from the library. The plot, the characters, the dialogue and the images are invented by you.
messages.- The story makes the central ideas of t: - The story makes the central ideas of the topic felt through events and characters, without lecturing.
messages.- Real people from the library act and s: - Real people from the library act and speak in line with what the library says about them; do not attribute invented views to them.
messages.- Do NOT put citations or page numbers i: - Do NOT put citations or page numbers inside the story.
messages.- At the very end write a line ## {0} an: - At the very end write a line ## {0} and under it the [[slug]] of every source or chapter whose ideas the text uses, one per line. The list is turned automatically into references.
messages.- NEVER mention in the text a “wiki”, a: - NEVER mention in the text a “wiki”, a “knowledge base” or folders and files.
messages.CREATIVITY 1 of 5 (strict): plain, preci: CREATIVITY 1 of 5 (strict): plain, precise language without images or metaphors; stay as close as possible to what the texts say, without your own interpretation.
messages.CREATIVITY 2 of 5 (restrained): clear, p: CREATIVITY 2 of 5 (restrained): clear, precise language with a little colour; connect the ideas only where the texts connect them; mark any interpretation as such.
messages.CREATIVITY 3 of 5 (balanced): lively lan: CREATIVITY 3 of 5 (balanced): lively language with some images and examples; your own interpretation and connections between the ideas are welcome when they follow from the texts.
messages.CREATIVITY 4 of 5 (free): expressive lan: CREATIVITY 4 of 5 (free): expressive language with metaphors and images; bold interpretations, an unusual angle and unexpected connections between the authors, as long as they rest on the texts.
messages.CREATIVITY 5 of 5 (bold): an original, d: CREATIVITY 5 of 5 (bold): an original, daring text with a strong voice, rich images and play with form; far-reaching interpretations and hypotheses are allowed when they are presented as your own reading.
messages.Creativity changes only the style and th: Creativity changes only the style and the interpretation: the facts, the claims of the authors and the citations come ONLY from the library at every level.
messages.In a literary text this level also sets: In a literary text this level also sets how freely the plot, the characters and the form are invented; the ideas and the facts still come only from the library.
messages.You are a careful writer who works from: You are a careful writer who works from the material of a personal knowledge library. The ideas, the facts and the citations come only from the material in the request; invent only what the request allows.
